## Pull request overview Adds Phase 5/6 “transformerless” evaluation primitives for (a) explicit resolution status + fallback policy (Decision D4 / Theorem 12) and (b) shortlist top‑M recall reporting with Gate H / Decision D5 trigger-gated fallback signaling, including CBOR report roundtrips to support certification artifacts for Issue #26. **Changes:** - Introduces `ResolutionStatus`, `CalibratedFeatures::classify()`, and `FallbackPolicy`/`FallbackAction` for D4 fallback semantics. - Implements `ShortlistEvaluator` + `ShortlistRecallReport`/`ShortlistMetrics` with CBOR serialization for Gate H-style shortlist recall reporting. - Adds integration tests covering classification/policy behavior and shortlist report metrics + CBOR roundtrip. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/shortlist_evaluator.rs | New evaluator/report types for shortlist recall + Gate H/D5 signals, with CBOR encode/decode. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/resolution_status.rs | New resolution-status classification + fallback policy types for Decision D4. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/mod.rs | Exposes the new transformerless modules. | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/shortlist_evaluator_test.rs | Integration tests for shortlist metrics, D5 trigger behavior, and CBOR roundtrip. | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/resolution_status_test.rs | Integration tests for Theorem 12-style classification and D4 fallback policy mapping. |

review_comments.body: The top-K recall loop scans each shortlist up to 6 times (`contains`, `first`, and multiple `take(k)` passes). This adds unnecessary work on large evaluation sets and risks subtle inconsistency if the list contains duplicates. You can compute the first match position once and derive all top-K counters from it.

`worst_routing_error` is computed over `min(scores_graph.len(), scores_teacher.len())`, which can silently under-estimate the max error when the vectors differ in length. Also, `(a - b).abs()` can overflow on extreme values. Consider treating length mismatch as an evaluation failure and computing diffs in a wider type.

`fallback_rate` and `conditional_direct_fidelity` are currently hard-coded (`0.25/0.05`) and set to `top1_recall`, which doesn’t reflect the actual observed evaluation outcomes described for Gate H certification (top-M recall, fallback rate, conditional fidelity without fallback). Also `worst_err <= 1000` is a magic threshold; using a named constant and deriving the other metrics from counts will make the report meaningful and auditable.
`self.calibrated_radius * 2` can overflow `u32` and wrap, which would misclassify very large radii. Using `saturating_mul(2)` avoids incorrect wraparound in boundary cases.

`self.score_margin.abs()` can overflow on `i32::MIN` (panic in debug / wrap in release depending on build), which would make `classify()` non-deterministic across build profiles. `unsigned_abs()` avoids this overflow while preserving the intended “magnitude < 10” check.
